hero.title: A Personal Desktop AI Assistant
hero.description: Friday brings a capable AI companion directly to your computer. It can understand the context you choose to share, organize the work around you, and turn everyday requests into completed outcomes.
hero.note: You choose the providers, connections, and permissions behind your assistant.

showcase.windowLabel: Friday desktop assistant creating a visual from a natural-language request
showcase.request: Create a cinematic launch visual from my notes. Keep it calm, human, and ready to share.

previousRequests.request: Give the launch a warmer, handcrafted visual direction.
previousRequests.assetAlt: Generated clockwork whale floating above a village

previousRequests.request: Now compose a short sound identity that feels curious and calm.
Turn the strongest direction into a quiet motion study.

demo.windowLabel: Friday desktop assistant handling a weekly planning request
demo.request: Plan the rest of my week, move anything flexible, and prepare me for Friday’s client review.
demo.response: I’ll use your current priorities and connected calendar, then keep an eye on changes.
demo.result: Two focus blocks protected, one flexible meeting moved, and a client brief scheduled for Friday morning.

personal.title: An assistant that grows with you.
personal.description: Friday can adapt to your routines, preferences, and priorities over time. The more useful context you choose to provide, the less repetitive setup stands between a request and a useful result.
personal.outcome: Less time keeping track of work. More attention for decisions, ideas, creativity, and people.

capabilities.title: Keeps useful context
capabilities.description: Remember preferences and relevant details across conversations, so you do not have to start from zero.

capabilities.title: Organizes what is ahead
capabilities.description: Bring schedules, appointments, reminders, and recurring plans into one working conversation.

capabilities.title: Continues in the background
capabilities.description: Let appropriate tasks run on a schedule without needing to supervise every step.

capabilities.title: Works with your tools
capabilities.description: Connect external services and information sources that are relevant to the task.

capabilities.title: Finds connected information
capabilities.description: Store and retrieve information through configured cloud services when the work requires it.

capabilities.title: Finishes multi-step work
capabilities.description: Move from a simple request through the necessary steps and come back with something useful.

workflow.title: Ask once. Stay in control.
workflow.description: Friday is designed to act on a request, not only answer it. You can follow the work as it happens, let suitable tasks continue in the background, and step in when an approval matters.

steps.title: Ask naturally
steps.description: Describe the outcome you want in your own words.

steps.title: Bring in context
steps.description: Friday uses relevant preferences, tools, files, and connected services.

steps.title: Let the work continue
steps.description: Appropriate tasks can keep moving in the background or on a schedule.

steps.title: Get a result
steps.description: Friday returns completed work or asks before a sensitive action.

workflow.approvalDescription: Friday pauses before an action that needs your decision.

extensions.title: One assistant. Many kinds of software.
extensions.description: Extensions give Friday focused tools, workflows, and interfaces while keeping the same core assistant experience. Start general, then shape Friday around the work that matters to you.

examples.title: Management
examples.description: Coordinate projects, organize teams, prepare reports, and follow up on work.

examples.title: Design
examples.description: Support research, creative exploration, asset creation, and design workflows.

examples.title: Architecture
examples.description: Develop concepts, organize project information, and assist with technical documentation.

examples.title: Entertainment
examples.description: Create interactive experiences, manage media, and support games or personal projects.

examples.title: Specialized work
examples.description: Connect industry-specific tools, data, and repeatable processes.

extensions.note: These are starting points, not limits. Friday is a foundation for the software each person needs.

control.title: Helpful should never feel intrusive.
control.description: Friday’s personalization is built around choices you make. Access, connections, and sensitive actions should stay visible and permission-based.

points.title: Choose what Friday can access
points.description: You decide which files, providers, and connected services are part of the setup.

points.title: Understand what is happening
points.description: Tool activity appears in the conversation, and sensitive file or command actions use permission controls.

points.title: Personalize at your pace
points.description: Useful context should reduce repetition without taking control away from you.

control.disclosureTitle: Connected work can leave your device.
control.disclosure: Friday stores core app data locally, but requested features may send prompts, attachments, source text, or tool data to the providers and services you configure.

cta.title: Start with an assistant. Shape it around your life and work.
cta.description: Let Friday handle more of the repetitive work, so you can stay focused on the parts that need your judgment, creativity, and care.
cta.platforms: Available for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

hero.eyebrow: Desktop AI copilot for macOS, Windows, and Linux
hero.title: Turn knowledge into action.
hero.description: Friday works with your files, tools, and chosen AI providers—then turns useful work into reusable Skills, grounded search, a source-aware LLM Wiki, and focused Extensions.
hero.note: Bring your own providers. Keep control of the setup. Follow every tool action in the conversation.

foundation.title: One assistant, from request to result.
foundation.description: Type or speak a request, attach images or PDFs, and let Friday work across files, commands, the web, browser interactions, and generated media. Tool activity streams into the conversation, while permission controls govern sensitive file and command actions.

providers.title: Choose the providers behind Friday.
providers.description: Friday ships 32 built-in provider manifests across chat, speech, media, embeddings, web search, vector retrieval, and object storage. Configure the services you want and keep each capability’s provider selection independent.
providers.note: Catalog and runtime coverage vary by capability.

skills.title: Teach Friday the way you work.
skills.description: Turn repeatable workflows into portable Agent Skills. Friday routes requests with lightweight skill metadata, loads the full instructions only when they are relevant, and can use the scripts, references, and assets bundled with each skill.
skills.callout: Full instructions arrive only when the task needs them—reusable expertise without placing every playbook into every prompt.

knowledge.title: Find the source. Keep the insight.
knowledge.description: Friday uses two complementary knowledge layers. The Knowledge Base retrieves relevant excerpts from indexed text. The LLM Wiki turns changing source material into structured, interlinked Markdown that can be checked, reviewed, and reused.
knowledge.baseDescription: Choose one or more folders of text, create a semantic index with your selected embedding provider and Pinecone, and let Friday retrieve matching excerpts with their source paths. Generate the index on demand, keep it refreshed on a schedule, and test searches directly in Settings.
knowledge.wikiTitle: Build knowledge that improves as sources change.
knowledge.wikiDescription: Compile Markdown, text, JSON, CSV, and log files into a persistent, interlinked Markdown wiki. Friday preserves source evidence, maintains traceable claims and contradictions, validates every staged update, and incrementally skips sources that have not changed.
knowledge.callout: The wiki gives Friday durable synthesis. Raw evidence and the Knowledge Base remain available when an answer needs exact wording or broader retrieval.
knowledge.comparisonTitle: Two knowledge layers, distinct by design.

extensions.title: Small apps. The full power of Friday.
extensions.description: Extensions are focused apps with access to Friday's AI agent and tools. Open a dedicated interface for events, notes, design, architecture, or any repeatable workflow while the same agent keeps the context and does the work.
extensions.trustDescription: Extensions run in Electron’s sandboxed web runtime, but installed code can access broad Friday APIs.

demo.agentDescription: Every extension shares the same agent, context, and permissioned tools.
demo.chatUser: Prepare launch week using the active extension.
demo.assistantIntro: I’ll inspect the extension context, check the workspace, and use the tools it exposes.

draw.title: A focused canvas, only for drawing.
draw.description: Draw is a dedicated extension for sketching, diagramming, and exploring visual ideas. It stays intentionally focused while remaining connected to Friday’s settings, agent, and tools.
draw.canvasHint: To move the canvas, hold the spacebar while dragging or use the hand tool
draw.drawHint: Pick a tool and start drawing!

control.title: Your setup. Your providers. Your control.
control.description: Friday stores provider keys, settings, conversations, workspace data, Skills, Extensions, and generated wiki files on the user’s machine. The user selects the providers and connected services behind chat, speech, media, search, embeddings, and knowledge generation.
control.disclosureTitle: Local storage is not the same as on-device processing.
control.disclosure: Local storage does not mean every operation stays on-device. Prompts, attachments, source text, document chunks, and tool data may be sent to the AI providers, Pinecone index, MCP servers, websites, or other connected services required for a requested feature.

cta.title: Build an assistant around the way you work.
cta.description: Start with a conversation. Add the skills, knowledge, providers, and extensions that make Friday yours.
cta.platforms: Available for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Open source under the MIT License.

skillPoints: Import agentskills.io-compatible folders built around SKILL.md.
Let Friday select an enabled skill by intent, or request one explicitly.
Inspect a skill's identity, authoring metadata, tool requirements, connectors, and tags.
Enable, disable, download, refresh, or delete local skills from Settings.
See a clear activity state in chat whenever Friday loads a skill.
knowledgeBasePoints: Recursively indexes readable UTF-8 text while skipping binary files.
Uses the same embedding model for indexing and later queries.
Gives the main assistant relevant excerpts, paths, and relevance scores.
Supports manual generation and scheduled full index rebuilds.
Rejects common credential files and high-confidence secret content before indexing.
wikiPoints: Generates concise source, concept, topic, project, comparison, synthesis, and question pages.
Records source-aware claims, confidence, relationships, contradictions, and open questions.
Keeps immutable evidence snapshots and an append-only operation log.
Stages and validates updates before atomically replacing the generated wiki.
Supports manual generation, cancellation, scheduled maintenance, linting, and review for major synthesis rewrites.
Stores the generated wiki as ordinary Markdown in a user-selected local folder.

extensionPoints: Import one or more extension folders from Settings.
Use a validated manifest.json or standard package.json with a local HTML entry.

Inspect metadata, open an extension in a dedicated resizable window, or delete it with confirmation.
Launch installed extensions from Settings, the native app menu, or the tray menu.

controlPoints: File writes, edits, patches, and command execution follow the agent permission policy.
Sensitive actions can surface Deny, Allow once, and Always allow choices.
Tool activity remains visible in the conversation.
The app uses Electron sandboxing, context isolation, disabled Node integration, and web security.
Friday runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux, with light, dark, and system themes.
